title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Ask for favours politely, make and accept invitations, offer things and refuse gracefully.
intro: Odia politeness is built into the verb: the respectful endings **-ନ୍ତୁ** and **-ବେ** already make a request courteous, and you can soften it further with **ଟିକେ** ('a little'), **ଦୟାକରି**, or by asking *could you…?* (**-ଇପାରିବେ?**). This unit also covers 'let's', 'let him/her' and 'may…' wishes.

vocab.en: Mr; sir (after a name); dear (to a boy)

vocab.note: With a negative: ଆଦୌ ନୁହେଁ 'not at all'.

phrases.en: Excuse me — could you listen a moment?
If it's no trouble for you…
Please come to our place next Sunday.
I'm sorry, I won't be able to come.

grammar.title: Polite requests: from 'do' to 'could you…?'
grammar.body:
From direct to very polite:
1. **କରନ୍ତୁ** — please do (formal imperative)
2. **ଦୟାକରି / ଟିକେ କରନ୍ତୁ** — kindly do / do a little
3. **କରିବେ?** — will you do? (future as a request)
4. **କରିପାରିବେ କି?** — could you do? (ability + question)

A very common addition is the helper verb **ଦେବା** ('give') after the -ଇ form, which marks the action as a favour *for someone*: ଲେଖିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ 'please write it down (for me)', କହିଦେବେ? 'would you tell me?', କରିଦେବି 'I'll do it for you'.

Asking permission: **…ପାରେ କି?** 'may I…?': ମୁଁ ଏଠି ବସିପାରେ କି?

examples.en: Would you help me a bit?

examples.native: ଆପଣ ମୋତେ ଟିକେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିପାରିବେ କି?
examples.roman: apôṇô mote ṭike sahajjyô kôriparibe ki?
examples.en: Could you help me a little?
Please write it down here for me.
Would you mind opening the window?

grammar.title: Let's…, shall I…?, let him…, may…
grammar.body:
**Let's**: ଚାଲ (*chalô*, 'come on') + the ଆମେ-future in **-ଇବା**: ଚାଲ, ଚା ପିଇବା 'let's have tea'.
**Shall I?**: the ମୁଁ-future as a question: ମୁଁ ଦୁଆର ଖୋଲିବି? 'shall I open the door?'
**Let him/her/them**, and wishes: the third-person imperative — **-ଉ** (ordinary: ସେ ଆସୁ 'let him come') or **-ନ୍ତୁ** (respectful/plural: ସେ ଆସନ୍ତୁ). This also gives blessings: ଭଗବାନ ଆପଣଙ୍କ ମଙ୍ଗଳ କରନ୍ତୁ 'may God bless you'.

**Refusing politely**: thank first, then a soft reason — ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଆଜି ଟିକେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ ଅଛି 'thanks, but I'm a bit busy today'. Offers of food are often refused once or twice out of modesty; hosts will insist (ଜୋର କରିବା).

examples.native: ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଆଜି ମୁଁ ଟିକେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ।
examples.roman: dhônnyôbadô, kintu aji muṃ ṭike byôstô.
examples.en: Thank you, but I'm a bit busy today.

dialogue.title: A wedding invitation
dialogue.setting: Mr Das, Sam's neighbour, comes to invite him to his daughter's wedding.

lines.speaker: Mr Das
lines.native: ସାମ୍ ବାବୁ, ଆସନ୍ତା ଶୁକ୍ରବାର ମୋ ଝିଅର ବାହାଘର। ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ କରିବାକୁ ଆସିଛି।
lines.roman: Sam babu, asônta sukrôbarô mo jhiôrô bahaghôrô. apôṇôṅku nimôntrôṇô kôribaku asichhi.
lines.en: Sam, my daughter's wedding is next Friday. I've come to invite you.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଅଭିନନ୍ଦନ, ଦାସ ବାବୁ! ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ପାଇଁ ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ।
lines.roman: ôbhinôndônô, Dasô babu! nimôntrôṇô paiṃ dhônnyôbadô.
lines.en: Congratulations, Mr Das! Thank you for the invitation.

lines.speaker: Mr Das
lines.native: ଆପଣ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବେ। ଏଇ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ପତ୍ର ନିଅନ୍ତୁ।
lines.roman: apôṇô nischôyô asibe. ei nimôntrôṇô pôtrô niôntu.
lines.en: You must come. Here, take the invitation card.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Of course I'll come. What time shall I come?

lines.speaker: Mr Das
lines.en: From seven in the evening. There's a feast at night.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୋର ଗୋଟିଏ ଅନୁରୋଧ ଅଛି। ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗ ବାପିଙ୍କୁ ସାଥିରେ ଆଣିପାରିବି କି?
lines.roman: morô goṭie ônurodhô ôchhi. mo saṅgô Bapiṅku sathire aṇiparibi ki?
lines.en: I have a request. May I bring my friend Bapi along?

lines.speaker: Mr Das
lines.native: ଅଲବତ୍! ଆଦୌ ଅସୁବିଧା ନାହିଁ। ଯେତେ ଲୋକ, ସେତେ ଖୁସି।
lines.roman: ôlôbôt! adôu ôsubidha nahiṃ. jete lokô, sete khusi.
lines.en: Of course! No trouble at all. The more the merrier.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ। ମୁଁ କ'ଣ ପିନ୍ଧିବି, ଟିକେ କହିଦେବେ?
lines.roman: dhônnyôbadô. muṃ kôṇô pindhibi, ṭike kôhidebe?
lines.en: Thank you. Could you tell me what I should wear?

lines.speaker: Mr Das
lines.en: Wear a dhoti and kurta — you'll look great!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Okay, I'll give it a try!

culture: Invitations to weddings and *thread ceremonies* are often delivered in person with a printed card, sometimes with a small sweet — and you are expected to come. Bring a gift or cash in an envelope (an amount ending in 1, like ₹501, is auspicious). Hosts will press food on you repeatedly; to stop, cover your plate with your hand and say **ନା ନା, ପେଟ ପୂରିଗଲା**. Younger people touch the feet of elders (ପାଦ ଛୁଇଁବା) to receive their blessing (ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ).

tip.title: Asking nicely
tip.body:
- Polite command: **କରନ୍ତୁ**. Softer: future question **କରିବେ?** Softest: **କରିପାରିବେ କି?** 'could you?'
- Add **ଦେବା** after the -ଇ form for a favour: କହି**ଦେବେ?** 'would you tell me?', ଲେଖି**ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ** 'write it down for me'.
- May I? **ମୁଁ … -ଇପାରେ କି?**

sentences.en: Could you tell me the way?
Could you speak a bit more slowly?
Please write your name down for me.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଏଠି ଟିକେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରିପାରେ କି?
sentences.roman: muṃ eṭhi ṭike ôpekhya kôripare ki?
sentences.en: May I wait here a while?
Would you mind switching on the fan?
May I come in?
Of course — have a seat.
Is this a bother for you?
No, not at all.

tip.title: Accepting and refusing
tip.body:
- Invite with the polite command: ଆମ ଘରକୁ **ଆସନ୍ତୁ**.
- Accept: **ମୁଁ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଆସିବି**, ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ପାଇଁ ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ.
- Refuse softly: thank first, then a reason with **କିନ୍ତୁ** — ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, କିନ୍ତୁ ମୁଁ ଟିକେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ.
- A flat **ନା** sounds rude.

sentences.native: ଶନିବାର ଆମ ଘରେ ଭୋଜି ଅଛି, ଆପଣ ଆସନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: sônibarô amô ghôre bhoji ôchhi, apôṇô asôntu.
sentences.en: There's a feast at our place on Saturday — please come.

sentences.native: ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଶନିବାର ମୁଁ ବହୁତ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ।
sentences.roman: dhônnyôbadô, kintu sônibarô muṃ bôhutô byôstô.
sentences.en: Thanks, but I'm very busy on Saturday.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ତୁମକୁ ମୋ ଜନ୍ମଦିନକୁ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ କରୁଛି।
sentences.roman: muṃ tumôku mo jônmôdinôku nimôntrôṇô kôruchhi.
sentences.en: I'm inviting you to my birthday.
You'll come, won't you?
We have guests coming today.
Give the guests some tea.
She accepted the invitation.
I couldn't say no.

tip.title: Shall I, let's, let him
tip.body:
- **Shall I?** — the ମୁଁ-future as a question: ମୁଁ ଚା ଆଣିବି?
- **Let's** — ଚାଲ + the ଆମେ-future: ଚାଲ, ଏକାଠି ଖାଇବା.
- **Let him / her** — **-ଉ** (ସେ ଆସୁ), or **-ନ୍ତୁ** for someone you respect (ସେ ବିଶ୍ରାମ ନିଅନ୍ତୁ).

sentences.en: Shall I bring you some tea?

sentences.native: ଚାଲ, ତାଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଉପହାର କିଣିବା।
sentences.roman: chalô, taṅkô paiṃ goṭie upôharô kiṇiba.
sentences.en: Let's buy her a present.
Shall I close the window?
Let him rest a while. (respectful)
Let him come, then we'll eat.
Let's eat together.

sentences.native: ଏହା ବହୁତ ଭଲ ସୁଯୋଗ, ଚାଲ ଯିବା।
sentences.roman: eha bôhutô bhôlô sujogô, chalô jiba.
sentences.en: It's a great chance — let's go.

sentences.native: ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ମିଠା ନିଅନ୍ତୁ, ନା କୁହନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ!
sentences.roman: au goṭie miṭha niôntu, na kuhôntu nahiṃ!
sentences.en: Have one more sweet — don't say no!
This present is for you.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଆଶା କରେ ତୁମେ ଶୀଘ୍ର ଭଲ ହୋଇଯିବ।
sentences.roman: muṃ asa kôre tume sighrô bhôlô hoijibô.
sentences.en: I hope you get well soon.
You look lovely today.

tip.title: Showing respect
tip.body:
- Add **ବାବୁ** after a man's name (ଦାସ ବାବୁ 'Mr Das'); **ମହାଶୟ** is formal 'sir'.
- Use **ଆପଣ** and the **-ନ୍ତି / -ନ୍ତୁ** forms with elders.
- Young people touch elders' feet (**ପାଦ ଛୁଇଁବା**) at festivals and greetings, and receive their **ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ**.

sentences.en: Mr Das, how are you?
The children touched Grandma's feet.
Grandma blessed us.
Sir, may I have your permission?
I'll ask Dad's permission and then go.

sentences.native: ଆମେ ଅତିଥିଙ୍କୁ ଭଗବାନ ପରି ସମ୍ମାନ କରୁ।
sentences.roman: ame ôtithiṅku Bhôgôbanô pôri sômmanô kôru.
sentences.en: We honour guests like gods.

sentences.native: ଜୋତା ପିନ୍ଧି ମନ୍ଦିର ଭିତରକୁ ଯାଅ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: jota pindhi môndirô bhitôrôku jaô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Don't go into the temple with your shoes on.
He treats everyone with respect.

tip.title: For …: ପାଇଁ
tip.body:
- **ପାଇଁ** 'for' comes *after* the noun: ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ **ପାଇଁ** ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ 'thanks for the invitation'.
- Same with wishes: ବିବାହ ପାଇଁ **ଅଭିନନ୍ଦନ** 'congratulations on the wedding', ଯାତ୍ରା ପାଇଁ **ଶୁଭେଚ୍ଛା** 'have a good trip'.
- With people: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ 'for you'.

sentences.en: Good luck with the new job!

sentences.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ମୁଁ ବହୁତ କୃତଜ୍ଞ।
sentences.roman: apôṇôṅkô sahajjyô paiṃ muṃ bôhutô krutôgyô.
sentences.en: I'm very grateful for your help.
Congratulations on your wedding!
Have a good trip!
Congratulations! You passed the exam.

sentences.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ନହେଲେ, ମୋତେ ଷ୍ଟେସନରେ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବେ?
sentences.roman: apôṇôṅku ôsubidha nôhele, mote sṭesônôre chhaṛidebe?
sentences.en: If it's no trouble, could you drop me at the station?

sentences.native: ତୁମକୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ନହେଲେ ମୁଁ କାଲି ଆସିବି।
sentences.roman: tumôku ôsubidha nôhele muṃ kali asibi.
sentences.en: If it's no trouble for you, I'll come tomorrow.

sentences.native: ଆମେ ଆପଣଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ସବୁଦିନ କୃତଜ୍ଞ ରହିବା।
sentences.roman: ame apôṇôṅkô pakhôre sôbudinô krutôgyô rôhiba.
sentences.en: We'll always be grateful to you.
